$comment: SHIPPED DEFAULT managed-process registry for a fresh installation.
src/lib/managed-processes.js loadRegistry() fails closed: a missing file
throws, and so does a registry that declares zero processes. That throw is
not lazy -- src/lib/owner-steps.js resolves four taskNames out of this
registry in a module-level const, so on a machine without this file the
require() of owner-steps.js throws, and with it owner-chat.js and
telegram-bridge-commands.js. Measured in a sterile payload run:
'managed-processes: registry file unreadable at <root>/config/managed-
processes.json'.
The builder's own registry cannot be the file that ships. It describes the
builder's fleet -- twenty-one processes, a sibling checkout of another repo
at ../AgentActivityVisualizer, retired owner-host scheduled-process records,
and a real Google Cloud project
id in the fleet-supervisor argv. None of that is true on a customer's
machine, and the account names and project id are personal data. They are
described here rather than quoted, because a file that explains an owner-
data leak by reproducing the owner data is still an owner-data leak -- the
packer's guard caught exactly that in the first draft of this comment.
So this file declares the four optional process records that modules in the
shipped payload need in order to load, plus the complete portable coordinator
duty host that keeps mechanical coordinator work alive between app sessions.
The registry is structural metadata, not proof that every optional process is
installed on a fresh machine. declaredArgv is empty for optional placeholders,
because inventing an argv -- particularly the
fleet-supervisor --project value, which is a real cloud project id -- would
be the same category of lie as shipping the builder's. Per-installation
setup may replace a placeholder only when it installs the complete process.
The three optional entry points are deliberately empty. The customer payload ships
neither the optional dashboard, the builder-oriented fleet supervisor
and its external Gemini contract inputs, nor a UAC helper registration path.
Shipping only the UAC JavaScript file would still be a false capability: a fresh
install has no registrar or packaged-runtime task action that can start it elevated.
Naming any source-tree path here would therefore advertise a program the install
cannot start. These placeholders exist only for task-name lookups in shipped
modules; setup may replace them only when it installs the complete process path.
The coordinator duty host is different: its JavaScript closure, fixed scheduled-
task registrar, and the registrar's PowerShell dependencies all ship together.
Its declared argv is exactly --serve, which keeps restart authority report-only
unless an operator explicitly asks the host for its separate bounded mode.
The owner-host entry is deliberately absent: the installed app starts and
stops its same-principal session authority in process. It is not a scheduled
managed process and no static account field participates in its authority.
